statement:
You are given a string `s` made up only of the bracket characters `(`, `)`, `{`, `}`, `[` and `]`. Decide whether it is **valid**.

A string is valid when every opening bracket is closed by a bracket of the same type, brackets are closed in the correct order (the most recently opened one closes first), and every closing bracket has a matching opener. Return `true` or `false`.

Push openers; on a closer, the stack must be non-empty and its top must be the matching opener (pop it). At the end, the stack must be empty.

solutions.name: Repeated Pair Removal
solutions.description: Keep deleting adjacent "()" pairs until none remain; every leftover parenthesis needs exactly one inserted partner.

solutions.name: Balance Counter (Optimal)
solutions.description: Track how many "(" are still open; a ")" with nothing open needs an inserted "(", and whatever stays open at the end needs a ")" each.

code.bash:
minAddToMakeValid() {
    local s=$1
    local open_count=0 inserts=0 i
    for (( i = 0; i < ${#s}; i++ )); do
        if [[ ${s:i:1} == '(' ]]; then
            (( open_count++ ))
        elif (( open_count > 0 )); then
            (( open_count-- ))
        else
            # Unmatched ')' needs an inserted '('
            (( inserts++ ))
        fi
    done
    echo "$(( inserts + open_count ))"
}

keyPoints: Add remaining open at the end

solutions.name: Brute Force
solutions.description: From every start, scan right tracking the balance; stop when it goes negative and record the length whenever it returns to zero.

code.bash:
longestValidParentheses() {
    local s=$1
    local n=${#s} best=0 i j bal
    for (( i = 0; i < n; i++ )); do
        bal=0
        for (( j = i; j < n; j++ )); do
            if [[ ${s:j:1} == '(' ]]; then (( bal++ )); else (( bal-- )); fi
            # More closers than openers: no balanced string starts at i past here
            (( bal < 0 )) && break
            (( bal == 0 && j - i + 1 > best )) && best=$(( j - i + 1 ))
        done
    done
    echo "$best"
}

solutions.name: Index Stack (Optimal)
solutions.description: Keep a stack of indices with a sentinel for the last unmatched ")"; each ")" pops its partner, and the distance to the new stack top is the length of the valid run ending here.

code.bash:
longestValidParentheses() {
    local s=$1
    # The stack bottom is the index just before the current valid run
    local -a stack=(-1)
    local best=0 i
    for (( i = 0; i < ${#s}; i++ )); do
        if [[ ${s:i:1} == '(' ]]; then
            stack+=("$i")
        else
            unset 'stack[-1]'
            if (( ${#stack[@]} == 0 )); then
                stack+=("$i")
            else
                (( i - stack[-1] > best )) && best=$(( i - stack[-1] ))
            fi
        fi
    done
    echo "$best"
}

solutions.name: Prefix Recount
solutions.description: For every position, count the "(" minus ")" in the prefix up to it to get the depth there, and keep the largest.

code.bash:
maxDepth() {
    local s=$1
    local n=${#s} best=0 i j depth c
    for (( i = 0; i < n; i++ )); do
        # Recount the depth after s[0..i] from scratch
        depth=0
        for (( j = 0; j <= i; j++ )); do
            c=${s:j:1}
            if [[ $c == '(' ]]; then
                (( depth++ ))
            elif [[ $c == ')' ]]; then
                (( depth-- ))
            fi
        done
        (( depth > best )) && best=$depth
    done
    echo "$best"
}

keyPoints: Depth at i = opens − closes so far

solutions.name: Running Depth (Optimal)
solutions.description: Walk once, adding one on "(" and subtracting one on ")"; the highest value reached is the maximum nesting depth.

code.bash:
maxDepth() {
    local s=$1
    local depth=0 best=0 i c
    for (( i = 0; i < ${#s}; i++ )); do
        c=${s:i:1}
        if [[ $c == '(' ]]; then
            (( depth++ ))
            (( depth > best )) && best=$depth
        elif [[ $c == ')' ]]; then
            (( depth-- ))
        fi
    done
    echo "$best"
}

solutions.name: Brute Force (String Replace)
solutions.description: Replace matching pairs repeatedly until no more matches are found.

solutions.name: Stack (Optimal)
solutions.description: Use a stack: push opening brackets, pop and match for closing brackets.

code.bash:
isValid() {
    local s=$1
    local -A mapping=( [')']='(' [']']='[' ['}']='{' )
    local -a stack=()
    local i c
    for (( i = 0; i < ${#s}; i++ )); do
        c=${s:i:1}
        if [[ -n ${mapping[$c]+x} ]]; then
            # A closer must match the most recent opener
            if (( ${#stack[@]} == 0 )) || [[ ${stack[-1]} != "${mapping[$c]}" ]]; then
                echo false
                return
            fi
            unset 'stack[-1]'
        else
            stack+=("$c")
        fi
    done
    if (( ${#stack[@]} == 0 )); then
        echo true
    else
        echo false
    fi
}

keyPoints: Stack must be empty at end
